Sable-on-ivory wolf-rampant banners hanging from every gatehouse corbel, the wolf's snarling maw stitched in silver thread catching torchlight.
Triangular gold-on-crimson pennants lining every battlement merlon, each bearing a crowned chalice sigil repeated forty times across the curtain wall.
A heraldic griffin-passant shield mounted above the main gate arch, rendered in teal-and-copper enamel on hammered bronze plate.
Silver-on-emerald tree-of-ages banners draping the great keep's eastern face, root-tendrils embroidered down to the tower's stone base.
Long scarlet pennants bearing a white sword-upright sigil snapping from all twelve spire-tips, sword-edges glinting with sewn metallic thread.
Dynastic amber-and-violet stripes painted across every tower base in three-foot bands, the house's crowned-eagle motif stamped at each stripe's midpoint.
Sculpted lion-head water-spouts ringing the keep parapet, each mane gilded in hammered gold-leaf and maw painted blood-crimson.
Captured enemy banners hung inverted from the barbican's outer face, their once-proud black-dragon-on-white now deliberately reversed in defeat.
Square jade-field house-banners bearing a silver chalice-and-flame emblem suspended between the twin gate towers on iron-rod frames.
Mourning black bunting trimmed in ash-grey wolf-claw embroidery draped across the parapet's full length, signaling the lord's funeral period.
A rival faction's amber pennant flying alongside the castle's own blue-and-silver eagle banner atop the watchtower, signaling fresh alliance.
Dragon-claw cornerstone carvings painted in obsidian-black lacquer with crimson talon-tips at every tower's foundation-corner visible from the approach road.
Festival garlands of gilded iron leaves wreathing the spires above silver-on-purple crown-sigil pennants celebrating the heir's coronation week.
Livery-painted curtain wall in alternating rust-red and bone-white vertical columns, each column centered with a stamped black bear-passant medallion.
A massive heraldic eagle-displayed sigil burned in gold pigment across the central keep door's full twelve-foot span, wings touching both doorframes.
Mismatched pennants from three allied factions crowding the barbican spires — wolf-silver, chalice-gold, and serpent-green flying in tangled proximity.
Coronation laurels woven from hammered-copper ivy mounted above the portcullis gate, framing a freshly carved crown-and-sword relief in pale limestone.
Pearl-and-sable heraldic shield panels set into the curtain wall at fifty-foot intervals, each displaying a coiled serpent-sigil in raised iron relief.
Long violet-on-gold pennants bearing an open-winged griffin emblem strung between spire-tips, spanning the inner courtyard in ceremonial diagonal lines.
Sculpted heraldic-bear statues flanking the main gate in charcoal-grey granite, each statue's chest-shield painted house-crimson with a white star-burst.
Teal-and-white diagonal livery stripes running the full height of the keep's southern face, interrupted only by the painted black moon-sigil at midpoint.
Heraldic shield carved into the main gate arch's keystone in high relief, the crowned-wolf motif painted gold-on-azure and re-gilded each spring.
Amber-on-black triangular pennants lining the inner wall walk, each displaying a skeletal hand-sigil stitched in bone-white thread at the flag's center.
Crimson house-banners bearing a silver stag-rampant sigil draped from iron rings bolted across the great hall's exterior facade facing the approach road.
Pale-gold-on-deep-green square banners hung from every gatehouse window bracket, the house's twin-sword-crossed emblem visible from a half-mile distant.
